title: 育儿与教育：死亡与丧失教育 — Day 37

questions.question: 孩子问「奶奶去哪了」，为什么不建议回答「奶奶睡着了」或「奶奶去很远的地方了」？
options: 这类说法太含糊，孩子会追问更多细节，让大人难以招架
年幼孩子会字面理解，可能怕睡觉或空等；而对死亡理解越完整，焦虑反而越低
孩子五岁以前根本无法理解死亡，所以说什么都没有区别
委婉语不符合大多数家庭的宗教信仰，孩子把它说出去之后，还可能在学校里被同学嘲笑
questions.explanation: 儿童约 5–7 岁才逐步建立成熟的死亡概念，此前会字面理解：说「睡着了」可能让他怕睡觉，说「走了」他会等她回来或觉得被抛弃。用「死了」这样的真词按他能懂的程度解释，研究发现理解越完整焦虑越低。年幼不等于说什么都一样，恰恰是字面理解让措辞格外要紧。
questions.question_en: When a child asks "Where did Grandma go?", why is it discouraged to answer "Grandma is sleeping" or "Grandma went far away"?
options_en: Such phrases are vague, so the child will press for more details the adult can't handle
Young children take words literally and may fear sleep or keep waiting; and the fuller a child's understanding of death, the lower the anxiety
Children under five can't understand death at all, so it makes no difference what you say
Euphemisms clash with most families' religious beliefs, and a child repeating them may get teased by classmates at school
questions.explanation_en: Children build a mature concept of death gradually around ages 5–7 and before that take words literally: "sleeping" can make them afraid of sleep, "went away" can make them wait or feel abandoned. Use a real word like "died" at their level; research finds fuller understanding goes with lower anxiety. Being young doesn't make wording irrelevant—literal thinking is exactly why it matters.

questions.question: 爷爷重病住院，家长想「别让孩子知道，免得吓着他」。按儿童丧亲研究，更好的做法是什么？
options: 完全不提，等孩子长大一些再告诉他，以免他过早承受压力
让孩子多陪伴和安慰难过的大人，借此学会坚强
坚持让孩子去医院拥抱、亲吻爷爷，哪怕他有些害怕，也要避免日后留下无法弥补的遗憾
用孩子能懂的话讲实情，把去不去探望、参不参加葬礼的选择交给他
questions.explanation: 被排除在外比被适度纳入制造更多焦虑：孩子的想象往往比现实更可怕，还常在信息真空里自责。Worden 的研究发现，事先被准备、被给予选择的孩子长期适应更好。强迫亲近害怕的病人，或让孩子反过来安慰大人，都是常见陷阱。
questions.question_en: Grandpa is seriously ill in hospital, and a parent wants to keep it from the child "so they won't be scared." According to childhood bereavement research, what's the better approach?
options_en: Say nothing until the child is older, so they don't carry the burden too early
Have the child spend time comforting the grieving adults, so they learn to be strong
Insist the child visit and hug and kiss Grandpa even if scared, to avoid an irreparable regret later
Tell the child the truth in words they understand, and let them choose whether to visit or attend the funeral
questions.explanation_en: Being shut out creates more anxiety than being appropriately included: children's imaginations are often worse than reality, and in an information vacuum they tend to blame themselves. Worden's study found that children who were prepared and given choices adjusted better long-term. Forcing closeness with a frightening patient, or making the child comfort adults, are common pitfalls.

questions.question: 按「持续联结」理论，陪伴孩子度过亲人离世的哀伤，目标应该是什么？
options: 引导孩子按顺序走完否认、愤怒、讨价还价等哀伤阶段，最终接受现实、彻底告别
帮助孩子尽快放下，切断与逝者的情感联系，回到正常生活
把与逝者的关系转化为能一直带着的内在联结，比如记得、谈起、保留物件
鼓励孩子表现得坚强，少提逝者以免反复揭开伤口
questions.explanation: 持续联结理论颠覆了「最终要放手」的旧模型：哀伤的目标不是切断，而是重建一种新的、内化的关系。孩子哭一阵玩一阵的「跳水坑」式哀伤是健康的；强迫坚强会把悲伤压到地下，再以肚子疼、噩梦等形式冒出来。
questions.question_en: According to continuing bonds theory, what should be the goal when helping a child grieve a family member's death?
options_en: Guide the child through the stages of grief—denial, anger, bargaining—in order, until they accept reality and say a final goodbye
Help the child let go quickly, cutting the emotional tie to the deceased and returning to normal life
Transform the relationship with the deceased into an inner bond the child can carry, through remembering, talking, and keeping objects
Encourage the child to be strong and mention the deceased less, so the wound isn't reopened
questions.explanation_en: Continuing bonds theory overturned the old "you must eventually let go" model: grief aims not to sever the tie but to rebuild a new, internalized relationship. A child's "puddle jumping"—crying one moment, playing the next—is healthy; pressure to be strong pushes grief underground, where it resurfaces as stomachaches or nightmares.
